name: Zimbabwean Sadza
description: Sadza is genuinely made differently from its East African cousin ugali, even though both are maize porridges - real sadza starts as a cold maize-meal paste that's brought to a boil, then MORE dry maize meal is beaten in vigorously (a technique with its own name, kumona) until the mixture pulls cleanly away from the pot's sides, a texture ugali's simpler one-step method doesn't produce.
steps_detailed: Whisk about a third of the cornmeal with 0.5 cup cold water into a smooth paste.
Bring 0.75 cup water to a boil, stir in the paste, and cook 3-4 minutes.

Gradually beat in the remaining dry cornmeal, a little at a time, stirring vigorously and continuously (kumona) to avoid lumps, until the mixture is very thick and pulls away from the sides of the pot.
Cover and cook on the lowest heat 8-10 minutes more, without stirring, to finish.

name: Zimbabwean Muriwo Une Dovi

name: Zimbabwean Nyama (Grilled Meat)
description: Nyama, grilled or braised meat, is central to Zimbabwean eating, typically served alongside sadza and greens.
steps_detailed: Rub the beef with the garlic and oil.
Grill over medium-high heat, turning, 12-15 minutes, until well charred and cooked through.

name: Zimbabwean Mazondo (Beef Trotters)
description: Mazondo, slow-simmered beef trotters, is a beloved Zimbabwean dish traditionally cooked for two to three hours until genuinely gelatinous - beef shank stands in here for a more widely available cut with a similar rich, gelatinous result from long cooking, though real trotters have a distinct texture this can't fully match.

ingredients_full.ingredient: Beef, chuck, short ribs, boneless, separable lean and fat, trimmed to 0" fat, all grades, raw

ingredients.ingredient: Beef, chuck, short ribs, boneless, separable lean and fat, trimmed to 0" fat, all grades, raw

steps_detailed: Combine the beef, garlic, onion, salt, and enough water to cover generously in a heavy pot.
Bring to a boil, then reduce to a gentle simmer, cover, and cook 2-2.5 hours, checking occasionally to top up water as needed, until completely fork-tender and the broth turns rich and gelatinous.
Skim any excess fat from the surface before serving.

name: Zimbabwean Dovi

Simmer 20-22 minutes until the chicken is tender and the sauce has thickened.

description: Simple fried fish, a common Zimbabwean dish especially near Lake Kariba, real technique patting the fish dry first so the flour coating actually sticks and crisps.

Fry, 3-4 minutes per side, until golden and cooked through.
